{{Short description|Simplicial object in the category of simplicial sets}}
In [[higher category theory]] in [[mathematics]], a '''bisimplicial set''' is a [[simplicial object]] in the [[category of simplicial sets]], which themselves are simplicial objects in the [[category of sets]]. Many concepts from [[homotopical algebra]], which studies simplicial sets, can be transported over to the study of bisimplicial sets, which for example includes [[Kan fibration|Kan fibrations]] and [[Kan complexes]].

== Definition ==
Bisimplicial sets are [[Simplicial object|simplicial objects]] in the [[category of simplicial sets]] <math>\mathbf{sSet}</math>, hence [[Functor|functors]] <math>\Delta^\mathrm{op}\rightarrow\mathbf{sSet}</math> with the [[simplex category]] <math>\Delta</math>. The category of bisimplicial sets is denoted:

: <math>\mathbf{bisSet}
:=\mathbf{Fun}(\Delta^\mathrm{op},\mathbf{sSet})
\cong\mathbf{Fun}((\Delta\times\Delta)^\mathrm{op},\mathbf{Set})</math>

Let <math>\operatorname{pr}_1,\operatorname{pr}_2\colon
\Delta\times\Delta\rightarrow\Delta</math> be the canonical projections, then there are induced functors <math>\operatorname{pr}_1^*,\operatorname{pr}_2^*\colon
\mathbf{sSet}\rightarrow\mathbf{bisSet}</math> by precomposition. For simplicial sets <math>X</math> and <math>Y</math>, there is a bisimplicial set <math>X\boxtimes Y</math>with:<ref name=":11">Cisinski 2019, 5.5.1.</ref>

: <math>X\boxtimes Y
=\operatorname{pr}_1^*(A)\times\operatorname{pr}_1^*(B),</math>
: <math>(X\boxtimes Y)_{m,n}
=X_m\times Y_n.</math>

Let <math>\delta\colon
\Delta\rightarrow\Delta\times\Delta</math> be the [[diagonal functor]], then there is an induced functor <math>\delta^*=\operatorname{diag}\colon
\mathbf{bisSet}\rightarrow\mathbf{sSet}</math> by precomposition. For a bisimplicial set <math>Z</math>, there is a simplicial set <math>\delta^*(Z)</math> with:<ref name=":11" />

: <math>\delta^*(Z)_n
=Z_{n,n}.</math>

== Adjoints ==
The diagonal <math>\delta^*=\operatorname{diag}\colon
\mathbf{bisSet}\rightarrow\mathbf{sSet}</math> has a left adjoint <math>\delta_!\colon
\mathbf{sSet}\rightarrow\mathbf{bisSet}</math> with <math>\delta_!\dashv\delta^*</math> and a right adjoint <math>\delta_*\colon
\mathbf{sSet}\rightarrow\mathbf{bisSet}</math> with <math>\delta^*\dashv\delta_*</math>.<ref>Cisinski 2019, 5.5.1.</ref>

Let <math>K</math> be a simplicial set. The functor <math>K\boxtimes-\colon
\mathbf{sSet}\rightarrow\mathbf{bisSet}</math> has a [[Adjoint functors|right adjoint]]:<ref name=":7">Cisinski 2019, 5.5.2.</ref>

: <math>{}^K-\colon
\mathbf{bisSet}\rightarrow\mathbf{sSet},
({}^KX)_n
:=\operatorname{Hom}(K\boxtimes\Delta^n,X)
=\varprojlim_{\Delta^m\rightarrow K}X_{m,n}.</math>

The functor <math>-\boxtimes K\colon
\mathbf{sSet}\rightarrow\mathbf{bisSet}</math> has a right adjoint:<ref name=":7" />

: <math>-^K\colon
\mathbf{bisSet}\rightarrow\mathbf{sSet},
(X^K)_m
:=\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta^n\boxtimes K,X)
=\varprojlim_{\Delta^n\rightarrow K}X_{m,n}.</math>

== Model structures ==
Model structures from the category of simplicial sets, with the most important being the [[Joyal model structure|Joyal]] and [[Kan–Quillen model structure]], can be transported over to the category of bisimplicial sets using the [[injective and projective model structure]]. But it is more useful to instead take the analog replacements of the morphisms <math>
\partial\Delta^n\rightarrow\Delta^n
</math> and <math>
\Lambda_k^n\rightarrow\Delta^n
</math>, which are:

: <math>
\partial\Delta^m\boxtimes\Delta^n\cup\Delta^m\boxtimes\partial\Delta^n\rightarrow\Delta^m\boxtimes\Delta^n,
</math>
: <math>
\Lambda_k^m\boxtimes\Delta^n\cup\Delta^m\boxtimes\partial\Delta^n\rightarrow\Delta^m\boxtimes\Delta^n,
</math>
: <math>
\partial\Delta^m\boxtimes\Delta^n\cup\Delta^m\boxtimes\Lambda_k^n\rightarrow\Delta^m\boxtimes\Delta^n
</math>

and which lead from Kan fibrations to ''bifibrations'', left/right fibrations to ''left/right bifibrations'', anodyne extensions to ''bi-anodyne extensions'', left/right anodyne extensions to ''left/right bi-anodyne extensions'' and Kan complexes to ''Kan bicomplexes''.<ref>Cisinski 2019, Definition 5.5.10.</ref>

== Properties ==

* The diagonal functor <math>\delta^*=\operatorname{diag}\colon
\mathbf{bisSet}\rightarrow\mathbf{sSet}</math> send left/right bi-anodyne extensions to left/right anodyne extensions.<ref>Cisinski 2019, Lemma 5.5.17.</ref>
* The diagonal functor <math>\delta_!\colon
\mathbf{sSet}\rightarrow\mathbf{bisSet}</math> send left/right anodyne extensions to left/right bi-anodyne extensions.<ref>Cisinski 2019, Corollary 5.5.25.</ref>
* For simplicial sets <math>X</math> and <math>Y</math>, one has an isomorphism of [[Slice category|slice categories]]:<ref name=":11" />
*: <math>(\Delta\times\Delta)/(A\boxtimes B)
\cong\Delta/A\times\Delta/B,</math>
*: <math>\delta^*(A\boxtimes B)
\cong A\times B. </math>
